newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul corn buyers seen sidelined after hasty buys.
newsitem.headline: Seoul corn buyers seen sidelined after hasty buys.

text.p: South Korean corn buyers are expected to hold back further purchases of corn until early November or until prices appear to fully bottom, traders and industry sources said on Tuesday.
South Korea's corn buyers purchased their requirements at around $170 a tonne on a cost-and-freight (C&F) basis, compared to current prices hovering just below $150 a tonne C&F, the traders said.
"Our clients had moved too early at the highest price level. They seemed to regret their hasty purchases," said a trader with a Seoul-based U.S. grain export company.

December corn futures on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) have plunged 26.3 percent from their record contract high of $3.89 a bushel on July 12. They traded at $2.86-3/4 a bushel in the CBOT's Project A system session on Tuesday.

"We expect (South) Korean corn and feed grain buyers to be on the sidelines for the time being as they have already covered their needs until next May shipments. And prices are expected to fall further," said a trader with Cheiljedang Corp.
This year South Korea imported 6.02 million tonnes of corn from January to August, up 2.9 percent from 5.85 million tonnes a year earlier.
South Korea imported a total of 8.88 million tonnes in the year to October 31, 1995 and the United States supplied 8.62 million tonnes of the total.
